RebuildTree collects expanded folder ids from the old items and restores them, so the tree no longer collapses on folder clicks, chips, sorts, F5 or scan end. The selection is always the shown folder's item or none. Removed: the always-true ReferenceEquals check, the double child sort and the duplicated or orphaned doc comments on BrowseQuery and FolderRollup.
A folder the data chooses (first visit, card click) also expands, so its subfolders show. An empty table shows a one-line kit EmptyState under the column headers instead of a blank area.

Scan again, Verify now and Copy path in the row menu, plus Shift+F5 and Ctrl+C, act on the selection (falling back to the clicked or focused row). Rows not painted yet load off the UI thread, and rescans are by id, one scope per watched folder. With the drawer open, Up and Down move it to the neighbouring file (BeginInvoke after the list moves its focus, guarded by Drawer.IsOpen).
A different folder, search or chip resets the table: scroll to the top, focus on row 0, selection cleared. A sort change or refresh keeps all three.

HandleRequest keeps the user's sort (`_query with {...}`). ShowBrowse loads once per card click or search: the view switch loads it, otherwise it reloads itself. The LibraryBrowseRequest comment is corrected.
BrowseData carries every watched folder's path (RootPaths). PathOf and the tree's Show in folder use it, and the stale `_library` lookup and the label fallback are deleted.

A new LibraryQueries.FileCounts counts all three chips in one aggregate query, using the same state and tier conditions as FileIds. Problems now leaves out Missing files, as All and OK do. The header search counts its chips in that one query instead of materialising three more id lists.

RootSummaries returns HealthyFiles (scanned files with no open finding: state IN (1,2) AND worst_severity = 0), the same rule KindSummaries now uses. The card's OK segment uses it instead of files minus findings.

LoadLibrary checks all watched folders together with one shared 2 s wait. A check that has not answered is reused by later loads, not restarted and not waited for again, so offline shares no longer stack blocked pool threads or delay each visit.

A card's Scan and the tree's Scan this folder ask before a large scan, as the header Scan does (Settings → General → Ask before large scans). They use the folder's own file count and size; the times are the watched folder's estimate scaled by its share of the bytes.
The header search matches file names only, as plan 09 says. Search results show each file's folder after its name; the cell text is cached in Store.
FolderRollup drops child folders with no present file below them (renamed, emptied or deleted on disk). The watched folder's own folder stays.
Name order and every tie-breaker use `f.name COLLATE NOCASE, f.id`, matching the tree's case-insensitive order.
LoadRowsAsync repaints only when rows came back, so ids whose rows are gone no longer cause a query-and-repaint loop (the verifier's one-line fix).
Each row's cell texts are built once in Store (`_cells`, which also replaces the separate `_problems` cache). FileSource.Fill only reads them, so painting allocates nothing.
Cards and the drop area react only to left clicks (and Enter/Space). A right-click on a card opens its more menu at the pointer.

In search mode the breadcrumb heading leads nowhere: BrowseCrumb returns while Search is set. RebuildTree always assigns the selection, null included, so BrowseCrumb never walks a node of a discarded tree.

Partly fixed: the breadcrumb now gets all the width left of the chips instead of width minus a fixed 320 px reserve (about 186 px instead of 100 at 1280 px with the drawer open). Cutting leading segments to an ellipsis needs Breadcrumb in TreeList.cs: see handoffs.
DropArea raises every dropped path, and the page opens the Add folder dialog for each in turn, waiting for one before the next.

Browse table keys: Ctrl+Enter runs the shared fix (the row menu's fix item now shows Ctrl+Enter); Delete moves to quarantine through dialog A when operations exist; Esc clears the selection (MainForm still closes the drawer first); F1 opens the focused file's rule (HelpRule override). Tree keys: Shift+F5 scans the folder and Alt+Enter shows it, both handled in ProcessCmdKey before the tree reads Alt+Enter as Enter.

Folder cards use the kit SeverityBar control (a '<tier>: <count>' tooltip per segment, an accessible name, clickable segments that open the folder in Browse), and the hand-painted `_bar`/`_segments` are deleted. The render matches the reference.
BrowseFolder carries RelPath (plus Files and Bytes). The tree scan and Show in folder use it, and FolderRelPath (which rebuilt the path from display labels) is deleted.
Partly fixed: Library's Scan again and Verify now scope text uses UiFormat.Plural ('1 file' / '{n} files'). DrawerActions and ScansData are other streams' files: see handoffs.

Ctrl+Z runs the Undo of the newest toast that offered one (an Ignore, a repair of this session), once. It never reaches back to a days-old repair in the journal. With nothing to undo it shows 'Nothing to undo'. The toast's own Undo and Ctrl+Z share a run-once wrapper (UiServices.TrackUndo/UndoLast). 'Scan a folder…' loads the enabled Library folders off the UI thread and shows them in a second menu below Scan. The chosen folder is scanned at the default depth, the same call a folder card's Scan makes. With one folder it scans at once; with none it says 'Add a folder first'.

A manual scan asked for while this window's scan runs is queued with a 'Scan queued' toast, as plan 05 specifies. It starts once no scan runs, including after a scheduled scan in another process that takes over. The rail badge, the bell and the Scan button counts now reload on Roots, Findings, Ignores, Notifications and Operations changes. F5 refreshes the page and the badges (RefreshAll).

Library's folder-card load, which Browse needs for root paths, therefore still applies when the header search opens Browse. Load failures the page does not handle reach the error handler through UiTask.Run.

Owned services are registered in creation order (database, runner, scan engine, updates) and disposed in reverse. The scan engine now stops, and records a run as stopped, while the database can still write.

Start-up maintenance runs crash recovery first. Every step (notification registration, Run value, quarantine purge, scheduled tasks, version record) runs in its own logged try/catch, so one failure no longer skips the steps after it.

Messages are queued and drained on the UI thread, so a link or a forwarded scheduled scan that arrives while the window is starting, or while its handle is recreated, is no longer dropped. A dev or portable copy no longer takes them over. Plan 13 is updated. The scheduled-task part is handed off (PlanHost.cs).

ShellActions.OpenFile on a missing or unreachable file shows a 'File not found · <name>' toast with Show in folder, posted back to the UI thread. CopyText shows 'Copied to the clipboard'. Its COR-DECODE row gets RestoreCopy as RecommendedFix when the INT-ROT row is in the same 200-row window, and Salvage ('Save a playable copy') when it is not. The row menu, Ctrl+Enter and the Fix… intersection then disagree with the drawer, and a Fix… over both rows drops Restore.

Run one query, `SELECT DISTINCT file_id FROM findings WHERE status = Open AND rule_id IN ('INT-ROT','GEN-UNREADABLE') AND file_id IN (…batch file ids)`, call FilesWithIndexedCopy on those files, and apply hasHealthyCopy to every row of those files, as LoadFileDetail does.

problems.title: Scan again on files in nested folders enumerates the same subtrees several times
problems.evidence: RescanAsync now makes one ScanScope per (RootId, RelDir) (67). ScanEngine.ProduceRootAsync runs once per scope and calls `enumerator.Enumerate(root.Path, scope.RelativeDirectory)`. TreeEnumerator.Enumerate (77-117) walks the whole subtree from startRelDir. Suppose a selection (for example Ctrl+A, then Scan again) holds a file at the root level and files in its subfolders. The whole root is enumerated for the root scope, and then every subfolder subtree is enumerated again for its own scope. MarkSeen is posted again for each repeated directory, `_seen` and the run's 'N seen' are inflated, and CountPresent and MarkOnlineAsync run once per scope. For leaf album folders the change is faster than the old one-pass-per-root scope. In the worst case the work is roughly double the old single pass.
problems.fix: For each root, drop any scope whose RelDir lies inside another selected scope's RelDir, and merge its file ids into the outer scope. Equivalently, use one scope at the common ancestor when the folders nest, and a root-level scope when a selected file sits at the root.

KitButton clicks on KeyDown of Space/Enter (Buttons.cs:290-296), auto-repeat included. A keyboard user who presses Space again to flip the switch back while it is disabled, or holds Space slightly too long, runs RunNowAsync and starts a scan of the plan's folders, possibly Deep over every folder. Re-enabling never returns focus to the switch, which also contradicts the 319 claim. The disable is not needed for correctness, because PlanReconciler.Gate already serialises reconciles and the last one reads the latest row.
problems.fix: Do not disable the switch. Let the static Gate do the serialising, and drop or queue a toggle that arrives while the row's change is pending (a per-row pending flag; revert Checked under _binding). If disabling stays, record toggle.ContainsFocus before disabling and call toggle.Focus() after re-enabling.

problems.title: A second process opening the library marks the live headless scan Interrupted (new RecordSkipped path; newly reachable via the window)
problems.evidence: Database.Open always runs MarkInterruptedRuns, `UPDATE runs SET status = Interrupted ... WHERE status = Running` (Database.cs:125, 307-315). The new RecordSkipped(AppState) (PlanHost.cs:175-190) opens the library from HeadlessLauncher.RunHere's engine-busy branch, that is, exactly while another process's scan is live. Headless scans now really run, so a window opened mid-run does the same. Until the live run's own finish update overwrites the row (Stores.cs:174), it reads Interrupted. Scans offers Continue (ScansData.cs:40), and pressing it is refused. The Schedule row shows 'Interrupted', and the Dashboard recommends continuing.
problems.fix: Handoff (Core, not owned): have Database.Open skip MarkInterruptedRuns while NamedMutexLock.IsHeldElsewhere(EngineName). A crashed run releases the mutex, so its row is still marked. Alternatively, let RecordSkipped add the bell row without the full Open recovery.

problems.title: Operations drawer can show a batch other than the selected one, and reopens after Esc
problems.evidence: OnSelectionChanged starts ShowBatchAsync on every selection change (each arrow key). After `await Task.Run(() => Journal.List(int.MaxValue, batchId))` it checks only `IsDisposed || _view != 1` (line 447), then binds and calls ShowDrawer. When the user arrows from a large batch to a small one, the slower query finishes last and the drawer shows the batch that is no longer selected. A drawer closed with Esc while a query runs is opened again.
problems.fix: Keep a request counter, or the last requested batch id. After the await, return unless this is the latest request and, for selection-driven calls, SelectedBatch()?.Id == batchId.

problems.title: Failed undo records are not recognised as undo rows and still show as operations
problems.evidence: IsUndo checks for the 'undo:' prefix in detail_json (line 87). OperationRunner.UndoAsync replaces detail_json with the error when an undo fails (`UpdateAsync(undoId, Failed, detailJson: ex.Message)`, OperationRunner.cs:380; COALESCE keeps a non-null value). A failed Restore, such as the case in ToolsPageTests, therefore appears in Operations as a new batch named after the original action ('Move to quarantine · 1 · Failed'). It also becomes the Operations card's Last with 'Can be undone: No'.
problems.fix: Keep the marker when an undo fails. That is a handoff to OperationRunner: write `"undo:" + id + " " + message`, or store the reason elsewhere. Then IsUndo's prefix test holds.

problems.title: Delete all… (new) is O(kept × journal) with no busy state
problems.evidence: Delete all… (line 64) passes every kept original to DeleteForGoodAsync, which calls OperationRunner.PurgeOneAsync per entry (line 375). Each call reads the whole journal (`Journal.List(int.MaxValue).FirstOrDefault(o => o.Id == operationId)`, OperationRunner.cs:422), which is N full journal reads for N originals. Nothing shows progress and the Quarantine buttons stay enabled meanwhile. The 308 evidence already flagged the per-call re-read; the new button multiplies it. Restore does the same through UndoAsync (OperationRunner.cs:305).
problems.fix: Handoff: look the operation up by id with a single-row query in PurgeOneAsync and UndoAsync. On the page, disable Restore, Delete for good and Delete all while one of them runs, and show it.

problems.title: LoadTools now reads every Done journal row and checks every backup file on each Tools load
problems.evidence: `database.Journal.List(int.MaxValue, status: Done)` (line 51) loads every Done row with all JSON columns, and Kept() then runs FileInfo.Exists on each backup path. This runs on every OnActivated, F5 and scan end while Tools is shown. Purged rows keep backup_path because Journal.UpdateAsync uses COALESCE (Stores.cs:345-346), so the nulls passed by PurgeOneAsync and PurgeAsync never clear it. The work grows with the whole history, and for a NAS library the checks go over SMB, since the quarantine sits under the root. With that share offline, every original ever purged is listed again with size '—', and Delete all tries all of them. The old read stopped at 500 rows.
problems.fix: Handoff (Stores and OperationRunner): add a Journal query for status Done AND backup_path IS NOT NULL that selects only the needed columns, and make the purge clear backup_path and undo_json (an explicit SET, not COALESCE).

problems.title: Preset double click can still add the plan twice

problems.title: PlanRunTests does not guard the engine-mutex fix it describes
problems.evidence: A_plan_runs_while_the_launcher_holds_the_engine_mutex passes a random mutex name to RunHere (line 47). RunPlan's engine takes 'Local\MediaVerifier.Engine.Run.<pid>'.
